coordinate_and_sign: xfront=-a,rear=+a;yright=+bs,left=-bs;cornerorderFR,FL,RR,RL;s=sign(x*y).Elevationz=h+x*theta+y*phi+s*w. Positive extra downward slope moment requires more upward reaction at positive coordinate.

equations.normalized_unknowns: q=[h,a*theta,bs*phi,w] metres; omitw for rigid frame
equations.rail_warp_mapping: For front/rear meanheight0 and symmetriccrosslevels:rear_crosslevel-front_crosslevel=4*bw*d/bs. d isNOTrailcrosslevel.

numerical_conditioning: Unknowns scaled to metres; normalized stiffness matrix checked positive definite and conditionnumber<=1e12 only as numerical diagnostic, NOT an engineering acceptance limit. Rigidwarp removesDOF rather than approximating infinity.
limitations: One isolated two-axle truck, four symmetric station locations with individually specified linear rates. Not a whole coach or two-truck/body torsion solution.

Equal-radius rigid wheelsets, prescribed rail heights, horizontal small-displacement vertical-force approximation. Wheel/rail profile, contact-normal directions, axle bending and bearing/guide constraints are not solved.
Rates are aggregate corner values; physical paired coils can aggregate only with equal displacement. No spring free length/preload/diameter/solid height, damper, stop or mount geometry is selected.
Heave/pitch/roll datum displacements are mathematical compression coordinates, NOT installed mount/floor heights. Pitch/roll are elevation slopes, not an assumed global CAD rotation convention.

Optional roll restraint acts against an imposed reference. Actual sidebearer gap/contact/preload/friction, body motion/second truck and CG-height/gravity/lateral/wind roll effects are absent. This is not a stability or comfort assessment.

Warp is one bilinear vertical mode with generalized stiffness N/m, NOT conventional torsional Nm/rad stiffness or a fabrication frame section. Free warp is an analytical limit, not an engineered equalizer.
No friction, damping, dynamics, longitudinal/brake torque, guide seizure, fatigue, stop impact or joint strength. Actual combined load cases remain required.
Nonpositive spring force or wheel vertical reaction invalidates the assumed contact regime. Diagnostic linear values remain visible; no clamping or detached-contact equilibrium is supplied.
Positive model contact is not a safety criterion. No allowable unloading ratio, flange-climb/adhesion rating, operating speed or track tolerance is assigned.

primary_context.title: Wheel Unloading of Rail Vehicles Due to Track Twist
primary_context.use: Primary abstract establishes vehicle-dependent twist/unloading mechanism; no historical numerical limits imported. Matrix/formulas here are independently derived analyst equations, not claimed to implement that report or a standard.
